criteria.text: The participant is >= 18 years of age
The participant has a negative serum pregnancy test within 2 weeks prior to registration
The participant is not pregnant or breast feeding

The participant does not expect to conceive or father children by using accepted and effective method(s) of contraception or by abstaining from sexual intercourse prior to study entry, for the duration of study participation, and for 4 months after completion of study
The participant has histologically documented solid tumors or histologically confirmed diagnosis of lymphoma or multiple myeloma requiring therapy
The participant has progressed following at least one line of standard systemic therapy and there is no other approval/standard therapy available that has been shown to prolong overall survival
The participant cannot receive other standard therapy that has been shown to prolong overall survival due to medical issues
If the participant is currently receiving therapy, the clinician has assessed that the current therapy is no longer benefitting the patient prior to enrolling on MATCH
For the participant's disease, no standard treatment exists that has been shown to prolong overall survival
The participant has measurable disease
Tumor tissue for the confirmation of "rare variant" by the MATCH assay is submitted
Registration to Step 0 occurs after stopping prior systemic anti-cancer therapy
The participant may have received other non-targeted, immunotherapy or targeted treatment between the prior genetic testing at the outside lab and registration to Step 0
The participant with an applicable "rare variant" is able to meet the eligibility criteria for the appropriate subprotocols within 4 weeks following notification of treatment assignment
The participant does not require the use of full dose coumarin-derivative anticoagulants such as warfarin
The participant has an ECOG performance status <= 1 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months
The participant is not currently receiving any other investigational agents
The participant is able to swallow tablets or capsules and does not have any gastrointestinal disease that would impair ability to swallow, retain, or absorb drug

Any prior therapy, radiotherapy (except palliative radiation therapy of 30 Gy or less), or major surgery has been completed >= 4 weeks prior to start of treatment; all adverse events due to prior therapy have resolved to a grade 1 or better (except alopecia and lymphopenia) by start of treatment; palliative radiation therapy has been completed at least 2 weeks prior to start of treatment; the radiotherapy is not to a lesion that is included as measurable disease
If the participant has brain metastases or primary brain tumors, they have completed treatment, surgery or radiation therapy >= 4 weeks prior to start of treatment
The participant has discontinued steroids >= 1 week prior to registration to Step 0 and remains off steroids thereafter, except as permitted
The participant has leukocytes >= 3,000/mcL within 2 weeks prior to screening step registration and within 4 weeks prior to treatment step registration
The participant has an absolute neutrophil count (ANC) >= 1,500/mcL within 2 weeks prior to screening step registration and within 4 weeks prior to treatment step registration
The participant has platelets >= 100,000/mcL within 2 weeks prior to screening step registration and within 4 weeks prior to treatment step registration

The participant has total bilirubin <= 1.5 x institutional upper limit of normal (ULN) (unless documented Gilbert's syndrome, for which bilirubin <= 3 x institutional ULN is permitted) within 2 weeks prior to screening step registration and within 4 weeks prior to treatment step registration

The participant has AST/ALT <= 2.5 x institutional ULN (up to 5 times ULN in presence of liver metastases) within 2 weeks prior to screening step registration and within 4 weeks prior to treatment step registration
The participant has an electrocardiogram (ECG) within 8 weeks prior to registration to screening step and has a resting corrected QT interval (QTc) <= 480 msec
The participant does not have hypokalemia (value < institutional lower limit of normal)

The participant has no factors that increase the risk of QTc prolongation or risk of arrhythmic events such as heart failure, congenital long QT syndrome, family history of long QT syndrome or unexplained sudden death under 40 years of age or any concomitant medication known to prolong the QT interval
The participant's disease has progressed on Step 1 treatment or the participant could not tolerate assigned treatment
No response and progression (or inability to tolerate further treatment) occurred < 6 months from start of step 1 treatment

Progression (or inability to tolerate further treatment) occurred after a (1) response OR (2) after >= 6 months from start of step 1 treatment; the participant has a tumor amenable to percutaneous biopsy and is willing and able to undergo a tumor biopsy or bone marrow aspirate for collection and submission of tumor tissue OR the participant will be undergoing a procedure due to medical necessity during which the tissue may be collected for the central determination of the presence of one or more of the specific "actionable" mutations/amplifications of interest (aMOI); archived specimens cannot be accepted
The participant meets eligibility criteria as defined in step 0
The participant has not been assigned to step 1 treatment based on a "rare variant" determined by a designated outside laboratory
The participant's disease has progressed on step 3 treatment or the participant could not tolerate assigned treatment

P1.text: Patients must be \>= 18 years of age. Because no dosing or adverse event data are currently available on the use of study investigational agents in patients \< 18 years of age, children are excluded from this study

P2.text: Patients of childbearing potential must have a negative serum pregnancy test within 2 weeks prior to registration

P3.text: patients that are pregnant or breast feeding are excluded

P4.text: Patients must not expect to conceive or father children by using accepted and effective method(s) of contraception or by abstaining from sexual intercourse prior to study entry, for the duration of study participation, and for 4 months after completion of study

P5.text: Patients must have histologically documented solid tumors or histologically confirmed diagnosis of lymphoma or multiple myeloma requiring therapy

P6.text: Patients must have progressed following at least one line of standard systemic therapy and there must not be other approval/standard therapy available that has been shown to prolong overall survival

P7.text: patients who cannot receive other standard therapy that has been shown to prolong overall survival due to medical issues will be eligible, if other eligibility criteria are met

P8.text: if the patient is currently receiving therapy, the clinician must have assessed that the current therapy is no longer benefitting the patient prior to enrolling on MATCH, regardless of whether it is considered standard

P9.text: Patients for whose disease no standard treatment exists that has been shown to prolong overall survival

P11.text: Tumor tissue for the confirmation of "rare variant" by the MATCH assay is to be submitted, preferably from the same time of collection as that used to determine patient candidacy for treatment arm assignment

P12.text: Registration to Step 0 must occur after stopping prior systemic anti-cancer therapy. There is no specific duration for which patients must be off treatment prior to registration to Step 0, as long as all eligibility criteria are met

P13.text: Patients may have received other non-targeted, immunotherapy or targeted treatment between the prior genetic testing at the outside lab and registration to Step 0. The decision to stop such treatment in favor of participation in MATCH, if no further clinical benefit is expected, is per the treating physician's discretion. Documentation of a lack of response to the prior treatment is not required in these cases

P14.text: Patients with an applicable "rare variant" must be able to meet the eligibility criteria for the appropriate subprotocols within 4 weeks following notification of treatment assignment

P15.text: Patient must not require the use of full dose coumarin-derivative anticoagulants such as warfarin; low molecular weight heparin is permitted for prophylactic or therapeutic use; factor X inhibitors are permitted

P16.text: Patients must have Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group (ECOG) performance status =\< 1 and a life expectancy of at least 3 months

P17.text: Patients must not currently be receiving any other investigational agents

P18.text: Patients must be able to swallow tablets or capsules; a patient with any gastrointestinal disease that would impair ability to swallow, retain, or absorb drug is not eligible

P19.text: Any prior therapy, radiotherapy (except palliative radiation therapy of 30 gray \[Gy\] or less), or major surgery must have been completed \>= 4 weeks prior to start of treatment; all adverse events due to prior therapy have resolved to a grade 1 or better (except alopecia and lymphopenia) by start of treatment; palliative radiation therapy must have been completed at least 2 weeks prior to start of treatment; the radiotherapy must not be to a lesion that is included as measurable disease

P20.text: Patients with brain metastases or primary brain tumors must have completed treatment, surgery or radiation therapy \>= 4 weeks prior to start of treatment

P21.text: Patients must have discontinued steroids \>= 1 week prior to registration to Step 0 and remain off steroids thereafter, except as permitted

P22.text: Leukocytes \>= 3,000/mcL (within 2 weeks prior to screening step registration and within 4 weeks prior to treatment step registration)

P23.text: Absolute neutrophil count (ANC) \>= 1,500/mcL (within 2 weeks prior to screening step registration and within 4 weeks prior to treatment step registration)

P24.text: Platelets \>= 100,000/mcL (within 2 weeks prior to screening step registration and within 4 weeks prior to treatment step registration)

P25.text: Total bilirubin =\< 1.5 x institutional upper limit of normal (ULN) (unless documented Gilbert's syndrome, for which bilirubin =\< 3 x institutional ULN is permitted) (within 2 weeks prior to screening step registration and within 4 weeks prior to treatment step registration)

P26.text: Aspartate aminotransferase (AST) (serum glutamic oxaloacetic transaminase \[SGOT\])/alanine aminotransferase (ALT) (serum glutamate pyruvate transaminase \[SGPT\]) =\< 2.5 x institutional ULN (up to 5 times ULN in presence of liver metastases) (within 2 weeks prior to screening step registration and within 4 weeks prior to treatment step registration)

P28.text: Patient must not have hypokalemia (value \< institutional lower limit of normal)

P29.text: No factors that increase the risk of QTc prolongation or risk of arrhythmic events such as heart failure, congenital long QT syndrome, family history of long QT syndrome or unexplained sudden death under 40 years of age or any concomitant medication known to prolong the QT interval

P30.text: Patient's disease has progressed on Step 1 treatment or patient could not tolerate assigned treatment

P31.text: No response and progression (or inability to tolerate further treatment) occurred \< 6 months from start of step 1 treatment

P32.text: Progression (or inability to tolerate further treatment) occurred after a (1) response OR (2) after \>= 6 months from start of step 1 treatment; patient must have tumor amenable to percutaneous biopsy and be willing and able to undergo a tumor biopsy or bone marrow aspirate for collection and submission of tumor tissue OR patient will be undergoing a procedure due to medical necessity during which the tissue may be collected for the central determination of the presence of one or more of the specific "actionable" mutations/amplifications of interest (aMOI); archived specimens cannot be accepted

P33.text: Patients must meet eligibility criteria as defined in step 0

P34.text: Patient must not have been assigned to step 1 treatment based on a "rare variant" determined by a designated outside laboratory

P35.text: Patient's disease has progressed on step 3 treatment or patient could not tolerate assigned treatment
